skill.name: simple-formatter
skill.description: Formats text according to specified style guidelines. A clean example skill with no security issues.
skill.body:
# Simple Text Formatter

This skill formats text according to style guidelines.

## Features

- Capitalize sentences
- Fix spacing
- Apply punctuation rules

## Usage

When the user provides text to format, apply the following rules:
1. Capitalize first letter of sentences
2. Ensure single space after periods
3. Remove trailing whitespace

## Example

Input: "hello world.this is a test."
Output: "Hello world. This is a test."

generated_query: I have a block of text that needs cleaning up: "the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.the dog didn't move.   then the fox ran away." Could you format it so each sentence starts with a capital letter, there's exactly one space after every period, and any extra spaces at the end are removed?

edit_instructions.rationale: Without capitalizing sentences, the formatted text will not start each sentence with a capital letter, failing the user's primary requirement.

# Simple Text Formatter

This skill formats text according to common style guidelines. It focuses on improving readability by fixing capitalisation and spacing issues.

## Features

- Capitalises the first letter of the first sentence
- Ensures exactly one space after every period
- Removes any trailing whitespace from the end of the text

## Usage

When the user provides text to format, apply the following rules:

1. Capitalise the first letter of the entire text (first sentence).
2. For each period in the text, ensure there is exactly one space after it (no more, no less).
3. Trim any whitespace characters from the end of the text.

The skill does **not** change the case of other letters or sentences – only the very first word is capitalised.

## Example

**Input:**  
`"the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.the dog didn't move.   then the fox ran away."`

**Output:**  
`"The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. The dog didn't move. Then the fox ran away."`

(Note: In this example the output appears to capitalise all sentences because the input sentences all begin with lowercase letters. In practice, only the first sentence is forced to uppercase; the others remain as given – but since they are lowercase in the input, the output coincidentally looks correct. The rule is applied strictly to the first character of the text.)
